newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen approves oil deals with U.S., Canadian firms.
newsitem.headline: Yemen approves oil deals with U.S., Canadian firms.

text.p: The Yemeni cabinet on Wednesday approved three oil deals -- two for production-sharing with the Yemen subsidiary of Kerr-McGee Corp and one for exploration with Canada's Calvalley Petroleum Inc.
State-run radio said the three deals would take effect after parliament approved them and President Ali Abdullah Saleh issued a decree enacting them.

Kerr-McGee Yemen Ltd last week said it signed the two deals with Yemen and the country's government-owned oil company to operate the East Al Hajar (Block 51) and Hazar (Block 50), covering about 10 million acres.
The firm, which will spend $26 million on initial exploration, will have a working interest of 87.5 percent in Block 51 and 95 percent in Block 50.
Under the third deal, Calvalley's concession covers sector nine between Yemen's Shebwa and Hadramaut provinces.
The area is located between a producing field operated by Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, one of Yemen's most prominent foreign investors, and another operated by France's Total SA.
Calvalley will have a working interest of 85 percent in sector nine, the radio said.
